collections.name: support_tickets
collections.description: Core collection for imported historical support tickets and any simulated incoming tickets used in the POV. This supports triage suggestion, similar-ticket retrieval, and dashboard analytics.

ticket_id.description: External/import identifier from the representative historical dataset or simulated POV dataset.

customer_account_tier.description: Ticket attribute explicitly mentioned in FR-1 and retained as a field rather than a separate collection because it is a small reporting/classification dimension.

manual_priority.description: Priority level manually set by agents in historical/current data. Optional because exact availability in every imported record is not guaranteed.

channel.description: Optional because POV review flagged channel availability as unconfirmed in exported data.

status.description: Minimal lifecycle state needed to distinguish resolved historical tickets used for similar-ticket retrieval and resolution-time analytics.

assigned_team_id.description: Reference to support_teams for historically assigned/resolved owner team if available in imported data.

triaged_at.description: Optional timestamp if available; useful for POV triage efficiency analysis but not required by the spec.

resolved_at.description: Present for resolved historical tickets and used to calculate resolution time metrics.

resolution.description: Embedded because resolution category and summary are described as attached outcome information for a ticket and are always consumed with that ticket in similar-ticket retrieval.

triage_suggestion.description: Embedded suggestion output for POV scoring and display. Embedded because suggestions are viewed in the context of a single ticket and do not need independent lifecycle for this POV.

text_embedding.description: Vector representation of ticket subject+description for semantic similar-ticket retrieval.

ingest_batch_id.description: Identifies the imported representative slice for repeatable POV loads.

is_historical_import.description: True for imported historical dataset, false for any simulated new POV tickets.

embedding_vs_reference.rationale: Resolution and suggestion outputs are tightly coupled to a ticket and read together with it. Support team is referenced to avoid duplicating team names across many tickets and to support analytics grouped by team metadata.

collections.name: support_teams
collections.description: Reference collection for the internal teams that tickets may be routed to and reported by in dashboard metrics.

team_id.description: Stable business identifier for import/demo mapping.

embedding_vs_reference.rationale: Separate collection because teams are reused across many tickets and are a routing/reporting dimension.

collections.name: dashboard_metric_snapshots
collections.description: Optional pre-aggregated metric snapshots to support live operational dashboards with fast reads if the POV chooses to materialize metrics instead of computing every chart directly from tickets.

dimension_key.description: For example a product line name, priority value, or support team id/name depending on metric.

embedding_vs_reference.rationale: Separate materialized read model only for dashboard access patterns. This avoids redesigning support_tickets while allowing low-latency chart reads for live dashboards.

relationship_summary: dashboard_metric_snapshots is derived from support_tickets and optionally support_teams, not a system-of-record entity
design_notes: Do not create separate collections for product_line, priority, or customer_account_tier in this POV because the spec only requires them as ticket attributes/reporting dimensions, not managed master data.
Channel is modeled as optional due to review warning that exported dataset availability is unconfirmed.

A single support_tickets collection is sufficient because the spec centers on imported historical tickets plus simulated current review; splitting into current and historical ticket collections would add complexity without a stated requirement.

dashboard_metric_snapshots is included as an optional materialized collection because the spec requires live dashboards, but downstream implementation may also query support_tickets directly for charts if acceptable at POV scale.
